text: Goal-directed queries are no longer hundreds of times slower than full evaluation on a large model asked many questions. A goal that knows none of its arguments now reads the relation itself, which the database derives once and keeps for every later query, instead of each query deriving a copy that holds every row anyway; a query that knows an argument of a relation the database already holds in full looks its rows up there; and a rule whose known argument sits inside a record pattern or a schema, such as `["claim", "?c", ["schema/open", {"topic": "?t"}]]`, runs as written and keeps the rows asked about, instead of scanning `claim` once for each value asked about. On the research model of Lion's own development, the 37 questions of its page took 36.6 seconds goal-directed and 0.12 seconds in full; they now take 0.11 seconds goal-directed. A host no longer needs `new LogicDatabase({ goalDirected: false })` for such a model.

A relation is derived the first time a goal reads it with an answer to extend, in goal-directed and full evaluation alike, so a query never fails on a relation that no answer reaches. With `["rule", ["report", "?t"], ["audit", "?t"], ["broken", "?t"]]` and no `audit` rows, `["query", ["report", "?t"]]` gives `[]` even when deriving `broken` would fail; it used to derive `broken` before running the rule, and fail.
